sentences.text: October nineteenth, twenty twenty-five. Nine thirty in the morning.
The Louvre has been open for half an hour.
On the riverside, a truck parks below the Apollo Gallery.
On its back is a furniture lift.
Two men in yellow work vests ride it up to a balcony window.
They cut through the glass with disc cutters, and step inside.
This room holds the French crown jewels.
The men smash two display cases, and take eight pieces.
Worth an estimated eighty-eight million euros.
They are inside for about four minutes.
Then they ride back down, and escape on motorbikes.
In the rush, they drop one piece outside: the crown of Empress Eugénie.
Days later, an old security audit surfaced.
In twenty fourteen, the password to the museum's video surveillance server was...
Police arrested the first suspects within a week.
But a year later, the jewels are still missing.
